description: Sample revocation-episode study records for PoPETs (Revocation-Complete Future Disclosure for Cached Longitudinal AI Contexts), conforming to research/venue2027/popets/protocols/study.schema.json. Positives validate; the single invalid_cases entry is an adversarial record the schema must reject fail-closed. Each record adjudicates one independent revocation episode under the future-dispatch noninterference predicate forbidden_label(g,p) ∩ lineage(d) = ∅ (threat_model.md §1): POPETS-CASE-02 is a fresh post-revocation dispatch whose lineage is clean (ADMIT), POPETS-CASE-03 is the revoked-then-dispatch re-disclosure witness where a cached summary derived from a revoked grant would leave the process boundary after t_r (REJECT of the dispatch, i.e. cancellation, never a leak), and POPETS-CASE-08 keeps INDETERMINATE for a dispatch whose assembly overlapped t_r so the event order is unknown and the outcome fails closed (never counted as a safe rejection). Decision vocabulary is evidence-handling only (ADMIT/REJECT/INDETERMINATE); measured outcomes such as the byte-level interceptor's future unauthorized disclosure rate belong to later phase artifacts, not to the schema record. All identities, timestamps and digests are synthetic research fixtures (source_authority SYNTHETIC_RESEARCH_ONLY).

cases.notes: Fresh post-revocation dispatch control (CASE_MATRIX POPETS-CASE-02, no retry reuse): consent for grant g purpose p was revoked at t_r recorded in the synthetic consent ledger, propagation completed within the declared Δ_max so t_e < t_d, and the candidate assembles the dispatch only from live source records under live-purpose permission clauses. The byte-level dispatch interceptor observes zero revoked labels in lineage(d), so forbidden_label(g,p) ∩ lineage(d) = ∅ holds and the episode ADMITs the dispatch. This is the authorized-utility companion that a correct invalidation must preserve; it is not a leak witness and asserts no erasure of anything delivered before t_r. episode_class=fresh_dispatch_after_revocation; lineage_verdict=disjoint; failure_mode=none; erasure_claim=none.

Revoked-then-dispatch re-disclosure witness (CASE_MATRIX POPETS-CASE-03 derived-summary chain, race R2 of threat_model.md §2): a field-derived cached summary of a summary whose origin- and purpose-labels are forbidden_label(g,p) was written by a pre-revocation read that landed in the derived cache after t_e, and a post-t_r dispatch consults it. The reverse-edge invalidation closure reaches the artifact, lineage(d) intersects forbidden_label(g,p), so the episode REJECTs the dispatch: the byte-level interceptor cancels it before the process boundary and no revoked synthetic canary byte leaves the process. This is a future-dispatch cancellation, not a leak, and carries no claim of retroactive erasure of bytes already delivered to the external provider before t_r (novelty_contract.md §5.4). episode_class=revoked_then_dispatch; lineage_verdict=intersects; failure_mode=interceptor_cancellation; erasure_claim=none.

Schedule-time race R1 (dispatch in flight at t_r, threat_model.md §2): the dispatch assembly overlapped the revocation instant, so the (logical_time, event_id) order of the cache-write and the ledger entry is unknown or contradictory and the state is INDETERMINATE per the timing model. The episode fails closed — the dispatch is blocked or freshly reconstructed from the live authorized view — and is counted in the per-arm indeterminate bucket, never as a safe rejection or successful completion. No coercion to ADMIT or REJECT is permitted until an independent adjudication resolves the ordering. episode_class=assembly_overlap_race; lineage_verdict=unknown; failure_mode=fail_closed; erasure_claim=none.

invalid_cases.reason_invalid: Fail-closed violations the venue schema must reject: observer is the wrong venue's adjudicator (leakage_auditor instead of re_disclosure_observer, ENUM_MISMATCH) and venue is another venue's const (acns instead of popets, CONST_MISMATCH), so a cross-venue record can never be silently accepted as a popets revocation episode. Additional independent violations each suffice on their own: silent nulls in the required unit_kind/backend/seed/branch/arm_id fields (TYPE_MISMATCH, disallowing silent nulls), a mechanism-outcome masquerade in observed_decision (LEAK_BLOCKED outside the enum, ENUM_MISMATCH), and an evidence array with zero pointers (MIN_ITEMS), so an unvalidated record can never be miscounted as a safe rejection.
